find:properties.notes:
Scope and count: I checked 280 non-empty displayed scalar values in data.json across 17 fields: bulk_density 32, bulk_density_range 10, specific_gravity 18, density_g_cm3 10, particle_size_d50 42, particle_size_mean_um 6, particle_size_distribution 37, cohesion 37, friction_angle 30, angle_of_repose 16, ph 11, magnetic_susceptibility 4, glass_content_percent 12, ti_content_percent 1, nasa_fom_score 2, particle_morphology 10, and particle_ruggedness 2 (also in PROP_CONFIG). simulant_extra.grain_size_mm is null for all 145 rows, so none is shown. One of the 280, EAC-1A glass 0.0, is hidden in every view by DataContext.tsx's `Number(x) || undefined`. NU-LHT-2M cohesion 0.0 is hidden in the right panel but shows as '0' in the table.

data.json matches lrs.sqlite for every exported value and all 560 property_sources rows. The export nulls 79 SQLite scalars that have no source row. A script flagged the doubtful values. I then read the sources: User's Guide Rev A Tables 7, 10, 19 and 22; the 2022 Lunar Simulant Assessment Tables 3 and 4; Roth 2025 LPSC; Ryu 2018 Table 5; LX Part 1 Tables 8 and 10, and LX Part 2 Sec. 2.2.5 and p.8; IGG-01 Table 7; the Engineering review Table 2; Liu 2024 Table 5; Zemeny 2024 Table 2; NAO-1 2009; CUMT-1 Table 3; PolyU-1 Table 6; the OPR data sheet; the Hispansion TLH-0/TLM-0 TDS; Linke 2022 Table A3.

Confirmed correct, no finding:
- Every Pa→kPa conversion (LX, TUBS 349.67/642.67/584.33 Pa).
- CUMT-1 d50 0.077 mm → 77 µm.
- EAC-1A d50 6.47 ϕ ≈ 11 µm.
- NU-LHT-2C 10 cm → 100000 µm.
- AGK-2010 and CHENOBI kg/l → g/cm³.
- Lumina 'dry unit weight' ranges. Their table header says g/cm3, and the text gives 9.26/15.43 kN/m³, which ÷ 9.81 = 0.94/1.57 g/cm³.
- All kPa cohesions from User's Guide Table 19, Stockstill Table 4 and Roth Table 4; FJS-1 8.13 kPa; TJ-1 D50 260 µm; ZJM-01 d50 19.26 µm.
- No magnitude outlier in any field.

Caveats I did not flag, because the unit is right:
- CUMT-1 and PolyU-1 'Density 3.45 / 3.17 g/cm³' are the dimensionless Gs values, also shown as SG. Gs × ρw is a valid conversion.
- Several specific_gravity values come from densities quoted in g/cm³ (JSC-1A, JSC-2A, TUBS-M/T, LMS-1E, OB-1, NAO-1, IGG-01, UoM-B). Numerically equivalent.
- TUBS cohesion is the yield-locus value at 3 kPa pre-shear stress; it rises to 1.9–2.8 kPa at 25 kPa. The page does not say which level.
- UoM-B cohesion is printed '3.43 ± 12.45' kPa in the source (SD larger than the mean).
- JSC-1 glass 50 % rests on 'half the volume of a typical particle is glass'.
- LX d50 is the dry-sieving value. The four methods give 63.7–536.6 µm.

findings.name: JSC-1A
findings.shown: Fe2O3 12.50 wt% and FeO 8.17 wt% in one table; Total 108.64
findings.stated: Table 1 (Weight %): 'Fe2O3 12.5', 'FeO 8.17', 'Total 108.64'. Text: Fe 'has been determined both by XRF and by titration'
findings.explanation: The two rows count the same iron twice. The other nine oxides plus Fe2O3 12.5 sum to 100.47, so 12.5 is total iron from XRF, and FeO 8.17 is the ferrous part from titration. findings.proposed: Show one iron row, never both summed: Fe2O3 12.5 as the XRF total iron (the oxides then close at 100.47) or FeO 8.17 from titration. If the page cannot say that 12.5 is total Fe, omit the Fe2O3 row.

The same bare '%' appears in src/components/table/SimulantTable.tsx:321 ({m.value_pct}%) and in src/components/panels/ComparisonPanel.tsx:135,140 ('Minerals (%)'), which puts different bases side by side as if comparable.

src/components/panels/MineralChart.tsx:140 passes no partialBelow, so src/components/panels/CompositionTable.tsx:73-74 prints 'Total' for partial mineral tables (BHLD20 45.00, NUW-LHT-5M 60.00, GRC-3 29.80, TUBS-T 97.00, FJS-1 92.85). The Total tooltip at CompositionTable.tsx:72-73 says 'as published by the source', but it is the page's own sum (CUG-1A shows 96.55 against the source's 99.8).

src/components/panels/ChemicalChart.tsx:26-29 and CompositionTable.tsx:36 add up every oxide row, including a total-iron row together with a ferrous row for the same sample (JSC-1A Fe2O3 12.5 + FeO 8.17 gives 108.64; NU-LHT-1M Fe2O3T 4.79 + FeO 3.3 gives 103.55). Nothing recognises that total-Fe (Fe2O3T/FeO*) and Fe(II) rows are alternatives.

Iron labels are ambiguous across the data. component_name 'FeO' or 'Fe2O3' carries total iron in some tables (CUMT-1 and CAS-1: 'Total Fe as FeO'; NUW-LHT-5M and LCATS-1: 'totals of each cation expressed as an oxide'; KIGAM-L1: '* Fe2O3 total'; JSC-1A 12.5) and a true ferrous/ferric split in others (JSC-1, JSC-1AF, NAO-1, FJS-1, KLS-1, OB-1). find:compositions.notes:
Scope and counts: I checked 545 displayed oxide rows (57 simulants), 228 displayed mineral rows (46 simulants), all 140 figures_of_merit rows (23 simulants) and the 2 nasa_fom_score scalars, 915 in all. I also scanned the 2 zero-valued oxide rows and 2 zero-valued mineral rows, which the panel hides.

Method:
- A script built per-simulant tables with their totals, value_text, the reference behind each row and the display string each row gets.
- For every row whose cited document is on disk, it checked that the number appears in that document's text: 683 of 773 composition values were found.
- I then read the doubtful ones in the documents themselves. These include JSC-1A Table 1, NU-LHT-1M Table 3, Gruener 2020, NUW-LHT-5M, the EAC-1A SI, Schrader 2010 Tables 2–3, Slabic 2024 Tables 7, 8, 23, 24 and 25, the CUMT-1 Tables 1–2, KLS-1 Tables 2 and 4, the CUG-1A, NAO-1, TUBS, BP-1 and PolyU-1 papers, the TLS-01 papers, the KIGAM-L1 Table 5, the review S2095268624001381 Table 3, the SRT/OPR/Hispansion sheets, and the simulantdb CLDS-i and CAS-1 pages.

What was clean:
- No oxide was stated in ppm or mol%, and none was stated as an element but shown as an oxide. Trace-element ppm tables were not imported.
- KLS-1's 'S 0.01' is total sulfur as the element. It is labelled S and its wt% is correct, but it is an element row in the oxide table.
- SRT, OPR and Hispansion tables match their sheets. LHS-2 'Fe2O3 3.20' is what the LHS-2 sheet prints; the LHS-1 sheet prints FeO 3.20.
- BH-1 Fe2O3 16.7 follows the 2025 corrigendum, which moved it from FeO; that is correct.
- MLS-1, NU-LHT-2M, NU-LHT-4M and the CSM oxides are Slabic Table 7's eight 'FoM-relevant' oxides, and their FeO is total Fe.

Documents not on disk:
- R086 (JSC-1, McKay 1994) and RN-S017-3 (EAC-1 thick films).
- R102 (JSC-2A). The two JSC-2A findings rest on its stored value_text.
- R104/R105 (LX): references_.local_path is empty, although datasheets/Lumina/Patzwald2025_ActaAstronautica_LX-simulant-system_Part1.pdf exists. Their value_text states wt.-%.

Minor, not unit problems:
- GreenSpar magnetic FoM shows '06' exactly as Slabic prints it.
- TJ-1 oxides come from a secondary review whose comparison table has visibly shifted rows (its 'Apollo 17' row carries Apollo 16 values), so TJ-1 reliability is doubtful.
- LZS-1 P2O5 2.0 matches the source as printed.
- CUG-1A's page total (96.55) omits its LOI 0.19.

The page has lunar-reference comparison columns, but every lunar_reference composition is null, so none display.

Owner's rule: where a unit or basis cannot be settled from the source, proposed = omit (JSC-2A Fe2O3, TLS-01 ilmenite and quartz, CUG-1A olivine and plagioclase). Where the source states the right value, I proposed only that value (GreenSpar plagioclase ~82 wt%, NUW-LHT-5M glass 40, BHLD20 synthetic agglutinates 35).

The relayed user request (show the version on the loading screen) is for the main session. This task was read-only, and I did not act on it or modify the repo.
